title: Move autoscroll preference behavior to recent
description:
Make whether or not we are autoscrolling a "recent" item.

Make the selection of automatically scrolling in the Capture
Options tab actually have an effect (right now it does nothing.)

Switching to a recent also means that the command line "-l" option
actually turns on automatic scrolling if the recent value is off
(currently it has no effect because it is always later overridden
by the preference value).

Document our behavior that autoscrolling, if turned on, temporarily
turns off when manually scrolling upwards or Go'ing directly to
a packet (so that a user can examine a chosen packet.) This temporary
effect does not change the "recent" status, which changes only when
the user directly turns the behavior on or off (through the capture
window, the button or menu item, or the -l command line option.)

notes.body:
added 25 commits
  • 5572d542...18018f75 - 24 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • 0dcc917b - Move most autoscroll preference behavior to recent
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/11675/diffs?diff_id=762157943&start_sha=5572d542d7f9b7e6b71c376fe9c9a49d81b426a3)

Perhaps this should completely get rid of the preference, and also have the behavior of whether autoscrolling (re-)starts when manually scrolling to the end of the packet list be set by the recent, i.e. whether we were scrolling when we started capture.

Either way, it is probably slightly confusing to users that the autoscroll behavior when turned on via the button during the capture when it was initially off is different than the autoscroll behavior if it was initially on. (Regarding whether it turns back on when scrolling to the bottom.)

 The preference _Interval between updates (ms)_ allows you to configure how often the packet list is updated during the packet capture process.
 A higher interval reduces processing, but causes more delay between capture and display in the packet list.
 
-Selecting _Automatic scrolling in live capture_ causes the packet list to scroll up once the packet list is full (see previous item).

 This might be a time consuming operation delaying the start of the program, however on most systems this is not an issue.
